## 1.3. Trends in Outcomes

Trends in self-labeling and depressive symptom severity over time in the raw data; this is important historical context for our research questions, and it also allows us to examine the functional form of our models below.

```{r descriptive-trends}
combined %>%
  mutate(
    dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("PIMH", "PIH")),
    `% currently self-labeling` = 100 * dep_self_label_now,
    `Mean DASS-21 depression sum` = depression_sum
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    c(`% currently self-labeling`, `Mean DASS-21 depression sum`),
    names_to = "measure", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = decimal_year, y = value)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, bs = "cs", k = 4)) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ dataset, scales = "free", space = "free_x", switch = "y") +
  facetted_pos_scales(y = list(
    measure == "% currently self-labeling" ~ scale_y_continuous(limits = c(20, 40)),
    measure == "Mean DASS-21 depression sum" ~ scale_y_continuous(limits = c(4, 8))
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026, expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside")
```

From these plots a few things are apparent:
* There is a significant discontinuity when data collection switched from PIMH to PIH; the sample got slightly less depressed.
* Depression symptom severity in our sample matches nationwide trends in young adults; rising over time, peaking during the pandemic, and reducing afterwards.
* Depression self-labeling follows a similar trend. If you look closely, you can see the self-labeling trends are slightly "tilted" upwards, i.e., have a stronger slope; that is reflected in the modeling below.

These plots give us a good sense of general trends, but it's hard to examine functional form from this. These plots do a better job; they're the raw data equivalent of the model plots below.

## 1.4. Functional Form, Visually

```{r examine-functional-form}
## Self-labeling by symptom severity by year
combined %>%
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("PIMH", "PIH"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = depression_sum, y = as.numeric(dep_self_label_now), color = year, group = year)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = F, linewidth = .7) +  
  facet_wrap(~ dataset) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(breaks = 2016:2026) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "DASS-21 depression sum", y = "% currently self-labeling", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

## Self-labeling by year by symptom severity
# Label severity bands
severity_labels <- c("Mild (DASS 5-6)", "Moderate (DASS 7-10)", "Severe (DASS 11-13)")

# Create severity-banded data
banded <- combined %>%
  mutate(
    dataset = factor(dataset, levels = c("PIMH", "PIH")),
    severity = case_when(
      between(depression_sum, 5, 6)   ~ severity_labels[1],
      between(depression_sum, 7, 10)  ~ severity_labels[2],
      between(depression_sum, 11, 13) ~ severity_labels[3]
    ),
    severity = factor(severity, levels = severity_labels),
    dep_self_label_now = as.numeric(dep_self_label_now)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(severity))

# Summarize by year
by_year <- banded %>%
  group_by(dataset, severity, year) %>%
  summarize(x = mean(decimal_year), p = mean(dep_self_label_now), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Plot
ggplot(banded, aes(x = decimal_year, y = dep_self_label_now, color = severity)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = F, linewidth = .7) +  
  geom_point(data = by_year, aes(x = x, y = p, size = n), alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_grid(. ~ dataset, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026, expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 3, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% currently self-labeling", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

These trends look monotonous (and perhaps linear) at lower levels of depressive symptoms, but less so at higher There may be a significant interaction effect in the PIMH sample.

## 1.5. Functional Form, Tested

```{r test-functional-form}
# Quadratic or cubic terms for time?
combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 2) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset) %>%
  summarize_models()

combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + poly(decimal_year_centered, 3) + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset) %>%
  summarize_models()
# No; relationship between time and self-labeling is linear on the log scale (as seen in plots above)

# Quadratic or cubic terms for depression symptom severity?
combined_model_dep1 <- combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
summarize_models(combined_model_dep1)

combined_model_dep2 <- combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 2) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
summarize_models(combined_model_dep2)

combined_model_dep3 <- combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
summarize_models(combined_model_dep3)

combined_model_dep4 <- combined_completed %>%
  fit_models(dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 4) + decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
summarize_models(combined_model_dep4)

# They are certainly significant - but do they make a difference for our predictions and ratios?
point_predictions(combined_model_dep1, c(2019, 2026))
point_predictions(combined_model_dep2, c(2019, 2026))
point_predictions(combined_model_dep3, c(2019, 2026))
point_predictions(combined_model_dep4, c(2019, 2026))
# Also yes (up to cubic)

# For risk ratios?
risk_ratios(combined_model_dep1)
risk_ratios(combined_model_dep2)
risk_ratios(combined_model_dep3)
risk_ratios(combined_model_dep4)
# Not really (a good sign for the robustness of our)

# Do they fit better, per BIC?
mean_bic <- function(fit_models) map_dbl(fit_models$analyses, BIC) %>% mean()
mean_bic(combined_model_dep1)
mean_bic(combined_model_dep2)
mean_bic(combined_model_dep3)
mean_bic(combined_model_dep4)
# Again, yes, up to cubic

# Interaction between time (centered around 2021) and depression symptom severity?
combined_model_year_by_dep1 <- fit_models(combined_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum * decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
combined_model_year_by_dep2 <- fit_models(combined_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 2) * decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
combined_model_year_by_dep3 <- fit_models(combined_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3) * decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)
combined_model_year_by_dep4 <- fit_models(combined_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 4) * decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset)

# Are the terms significant?
summarize_models(combined_model_year_by_dep1, exp = F)
summarize_models(combined_model_year_by_dep2, exp = F)
summarize_models(combined_model_year_by_dep3, exp = F)

# Do they change predictions?
point_predictions(combined_model_year_by_dep1, c(2016, 2026), print = T)
point_predictions(combined_model_year_by_dep2, c(2016, 2026), print = T)
point_predictions(combined_model_year_by_dep3, c(2016, 2026), print = T)

# Do they change risk ratios?
risk_ratios(combined_model_year_by_dep1, print = T)
risk_ratios(combined_model_year_by_dep2, print = T)
risk_ratios(combined_model_year_by_dep3, print = T)

# Do they improve fit, per BIC?
mean_bic(combined_model_year_by_dep1)
mean_bic(combined_model_year_by_dep2)
mean_bic(combined_model_year_by_dep3)
mean_bic(combined_model_year_by_dep4)
# All also point to an interaction at the cubic level
```

# 2. Primary Analysis

The preregistered primary analysis model is `dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year + age + race + gender + education`.

Per the above analyses, the functional form is better represented by the functions:
* PIMH: `...`
* PIH: `...`
* Combined: `...`

For the primary analysis, we use the best-fit functions above. We report findings from simpler, preregistered models in `Supporting Analyses.Rmd`.

## 2.1. Primary Regression Results

```{r primary-regressions}
# PIMH
pimh_model_primary <- fit_models(pimh_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year + age + race_recoded + gender + education)
summarize_models(pimh_model_primary)
point_predictions(pimh_model_primary, 2016:2019)
risk_ratios(pimh_model_primary)

# PIH
pih_model_primary <- fit_models(pih_completed, dep_self_label_now ~ depression_sum + decimal_year + age + race_recoded + gender + education)
summarize_models(pih_model_primary)
point_predictions(pih_model_primary, 2019:2026)
risk_ratios(pih_model_primary)

# Combined, best-fit (i.e., incorporates above considerations)
best_fit_model_base <- "dep_self_label_now ~ poly(depression_sum, 3) * decimal_year_centered + age + race_recoded + gender + education + dataset"
combined_model_primary <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base))
summarize_models(combined_model_primary)
point_predictions(combined_model_primary, c(2016, 2026), print = T)
risk_ratios(combined_model_primary, print = T)
```

### 2.1.1. Primary Regression Results, Visualized

```{r primary-regressions-visualized}
## Shared settings
severity_labels <- c(
  "5.5" = "Low (DASS = 5.5)",
  "8.5" = "Medium (DASS = 8.5)",
  "12"  = "High (DASS = 12)"
)

label_severity <- function(x) factor(severity_labels[as.character(x)], levels = severity_labels)

label_study_period <- function(dataset) {
  recode_values(
    dataset,
    "PIMH" ~ "2016-2019 Study Period",
    "PIH" ~ "2019-2026 Study Period"
  )
}

transition_date <- decimal_date(as_date("2019-08-21")) # First day of PIH data


## Plot 1: Separate models, faceted by study period
pred_by_period <- bind_rows(
  as_tibble(pred_pimh) %>% mutate(dataset = "PIMH"),
  as_tibble(pred_pih) %>% mutate(dataset = "PIH")
) %>%
  mutate(
    study_period = label_study_period(dataset),
    severity = label_severity(depression_sum)
  )

pred_by_period %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = decimal_year, y = estimate, color = severity, fill = severity)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = .2, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(. ~ study_period, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026, expand = expansion(add = .25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Predicted probability of self-labeling",
    color = "Symptom severity",
    fill = "Symptom severity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")


## Plot 2: Combined model
pred_combined_plot <- as_tibble(pred_combined) %>%
  mutate(severity = label_severity(depression_sum))

period_labels <- tibble(
  dataset = c("PIMH", "PIH"),
  x = c(mean(c(2016, transition_date)), mean(c(transition_date, 2026)))
) %>%
  mutate(study_period = label_study_period(dataset))

pred_combined_plot %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = decimal_year, y = estimate, color = severity, fill = severity)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = transition_date, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_text(
    data = period_labels,
    aes(x = x, y = Inf, label = study_period),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = 1.5, size = 3.5, color = "grey30"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = .2, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2016:2026) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Predicted probability of self-labeling",
    color = "Symptom severity",
    fill = "Symptom severity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r sl-by-ss-by-yr} 
## Response curve: first vs. last observed date (combined model)
date_endpoints <- range(combined$decimal_year)

pred_curve <- avg_predictions(
  model_combined,
  newdata = datagrid(
    depression_sum = 0:21,
    decimal_year = date_endpoints,
    grid_type = "counterfactual"
  ),
  by = c("depression_sum", "decimal_year")
) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    date_label = format(date_decimal(decimal_year), "%B %Y"),
    date_label = fct_reorder(date_label, decimal_year)
  )

pred_curve %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = depression_sum, y = estimate, color = date_label, fill = date_label)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = .2, color = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 21, 3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "DASS-21 depression sum",
    y = "Predicted probability of self-labeling",
    color = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 2.2. Moderation of Primary Regression Results

Will need to think through age. This is why APC is important. It looks like shifts over time are driven by older participants - but participants are also getting older...! Also this doesn't change that concept breadth is wider for younger people, too... so maybe changing less in this period, but already changed a lot?

```{r, primary-regression-moderation}
combined_model_moderation_age <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base %+% "+ age:decimal_year_centered"))
risk_ratios(combined_model_moderation_age, moderator = "age", moderator_values = c(20, 40, 60), severity = 8.5, print = T)

combined_model_moderation_race <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base %+% "+ race_recoded:decimal_year_centered"))
risk_ratios(combined_model_moderation_race, moderator = "race_recoded", severity = 8.5, print = T)

combined_model_moderation_gender <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base %+% "+ gender:decimal_year_centered"))
risk_ratios(combined_model_moderation_gender, moderator = "gender", severity = 8.5, print = T)

combined_model_moderation_education <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base %+% "+ education:decimal_year_centered"))
risk_ratios(combined_model_moderation_education, moderator = "education", severity = 8.5, print = T)

combined_model_moderation_dem_vote_share <- fit_models(combined_completed, as.formula(best_fit_model_base %+% "+ dem_vote_share + dem_vote_share:decimal_year_centered"))
risk_ratios(combined_model_moderation_dem_vote_share, moderator = "dem_vote_share", moderator_values = c(.25, .5, .75), severity = 8.5, print = T)
```

# 4. Robustness Checks

Robustness checks are reported in the folder `Robustness Checks/`. They include:
* Primary analyses using simple preregistered models
* Primary analyses using complete cases
* Primary analyses controlling for `referral_recoded`
* Robustness checks around age findings, including:
  * Age findings, controlling for `referral_recoded`
  * Age findings, binned (18-22, 25+)
